content.title: JPMorgan's Dimon: Credit card cap would lead to 'economic disaster'
content.description:
One moment that stood out in JPMorgan Chase (JPM) CEO Jamie Dimon's interview at the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos, Switzerland, on Wednesday was when he referred to himself as a "globalist," making light of President Trump's own comments calling the big bank executive "a highly overrated globalist.

Yahoo Finance Senior Bank Reporter David Hollerith highlights the top takeaways from Dimon's remarks, sharing his thoughts on the Trump administration's policy proposals on credit card rate caps and the broader banking industry.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Domination.

content.title: JPMorgan's Dimon on why the Fed isn't as independent as people think
Credit card rate cap would be an 'economic disaster,' Dimon says
JPMorgan will likely have fewer employees in 5 years, CEO Dimon says
content.description:
At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, JPMorgan Chase (JPM) CEO Jamie Dimon spoke about the impact AI will have on the global workforce and what companies and governments can do to help. Toward the end of the conversation, he was asked about jobs at JPMorgan Chase, and Dimon admitted that his "guess" is that the banking giant will have fewer employees in five years than it does today.

Watch Dimon's full World Economic Forum discussion.

content.title: Trump credit card cap would cause once in a lifetime battle from banks
content.description:
While major bank stocks fall after reporting their fourth quarter earnings, President Trump's suggested 10% cap on credit card ratescontinues to weigh on the financial sector (XLF) and credit lenders. HSBC Head of US Financials Research Saul Martinez told Yahoo Finance on Tuesday that a policy like this would make the credit card industry largely "unprofitable."

Whalen Global Advisors Chairman Chris Whalen explains how bank executives would respond to this type of legislation.

Also catch Chris Whalen weigh in on the performance of Big Bank stocks in comparison to smaller counterparts.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Catalysts.
